tagline: Shaping the digital future through integrated telecommunications and cloud solutions.
hero_kpi_rationale: Service revenue is the core pillar of Deutsche Telekom's business, representing nearly 83% of total revenue in 2025. It is the most stable and strategic segment, driven by mobile and fixed-line growth, particularly through T-Mobile US.

kpis.name: Service Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from telecom services (mobile, internet, fixed).
kpis.description: Service revenue grows by 2.9% in 2025, driven by T-Mobile US and fiber expansion in Germany.

kpis.name: EBITDA after lease (adjusted)
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit after lease, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA AL increases for the third consecutive year, supported by synergies and cost management.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow after lease
kpis.explanation: Cash flow available after investments, excluding dividends and spectrum.
kpis.description: FCF AL increases slightly, reflecting capex discipline and strong cash generation.
kpis.signal: Ability to generate cash despite heavy investments.

kpis.name: Net Revenue
kpis.description: Net revenue reaches €119.1 billion, driven by international operations (78% of total).
kpis.signal: Stable growth despite a competitive environment.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures (excluding spectrum)
kpis.explanation: Spending on infrastructure (networks, fiber), excluding frequency licenses.
kpis.description: Capex declines slightly, with a focus on spending efficiency.

kpis.name: Headcount (FTE)
kpis.explanation: Average number of full-time equivalent employees.
kpis.description: Average headcount declines slightly, despite growth in the United States.
kpis.signal: Slight contraction, consistent with digitalization and automation.

kpis.name: CO2 Emissions (Scope 1+2)
kpis.description: Emissions decrease by 4.9%, due to energy efficiency and renewable energy adoption.
kpis.signal: Ongoing emissions reduction, aligned with climate targets.

kpis.name: Revenue segment United States (TMUS)
kpis.explanation: Measures revenue generated by Deutsche Telekom in the United States through its subsidiary TMUS, reflecting U.S. business performance.

kpis.name: Adj. EBITDA AL Germany
kpis.explanation: Measures Deutsche Telekom's adjusted operating profit in Germany, excluding non-recurring items.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.986 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $6.438 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 67.0% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Mobile Customers
kpis.explanation: Total number of mobile customers worldwide.
kpis.description: Mobile customer base grows by 4.5%, driven by T-Mobile US and customer acquisition strategy.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in the United States with T-Mobile.

kpis.name: Energy Consumption
kpis.explanation: Electricity used by networks and data centers.
kpis.description: Energy consumption is nearly stable, despite growing data traffic.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Workforce transformation and large-scale social restructuring
risks.summary: Deutsche Telekom is implementing a workforce transformation program (2025 Workforce Transformation) involving the reduction of management layers and elimination of redundant roles. Provisions for severance and early retirement reach EUR 1.56 billion at end-2025, indicating persistent social and operational risks, particularly in Germany where civil servant status (Beamte) complicates restructuring.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in provisions (EUR 1.56 billion restructuring provisions as of 12/31/2025, up EUR 0.2 billion), with an active 2025 Workforce Transformation program aimed at centralizing teams and eliminating redundancies. Trend stable/increasing over multiple fiscal years.

risks.title: Broadband deployment obligations linked to public subsidies
risks.summary: Deutsche Telekom carries EUR 1.56 billion in liabilities related to broadband deployment projects funded by public funds in Germany. Failure to meet coverage or contractual deadlines could result in subsidy repayments and regulatory penalties, amid strong political pressure on national connectivity.
risks.score_rationale: Liabilities related to publicly funded projects increased by EUR 0.2 billion to EUR 1.56 billion, reflecting fiber/broadband deployment obligations conditional on subsidies yet to be received. Regulatory and execution risk in case of failure to meet contractual milestones.

risks.title: Integration and operational risks from the UScellular acquisition
risks.summary: The acquisition of UScellular by T-Mobile US generates immediate accounting impacts (restoration provisions, customer contracts) and exposes Deutsche Telekom to technological, cultural, and regulatory integration risks in the United States. Any integration failure could weigh on the profitability of the U.S. segment, the group's growth engine.
risks.score_rationale: The UScellular acquisition is cited multiple times as a source of increased provisions (site restoration +EUR 0.2 billion, customer contracts +EUR 0.2 billion). A recent transaction generating significant integration risks in the U.S. segment, already the largest contributor to group revenue.

risks.title: Exposure to litigation and rising legal provisions
risks.summary: Deutsche Telekom's litigation provisions increased to EUR 623 million in 2025, reflecting the group's exposure to multiple legal proceedings across its geographies (Germany, United States, Eastern Europe). These may include competitive disputes, customer claims, or regulatory disagreements.
risks.score_rationale: Litigation risk provisions amount to EUR 623 million at end-2025 (vs EUR 527 million at end-2024), an increase of EUR 96 million, related to potential settlements of ongoing legal proceedings. Upward trend during the fiscal year, without details on underlying cases.

risks.title: Structural dependency on civil servant pension obligations
risks.summary: As the successor to Deutsche Bundespost, Deutsche Telekom bears legal obligations toward active and retired civil servants (Beamte), representing EUR 212 million in annual contributions and EUR 0.4 billion in future liabilities. Any legislative change to the civil service regime or increase in affected employees would加重 these fixed costs.
risks.score_rationale: Deutsche Telekom pays EUR 212 million annually to the Civil Service Pension Fund and carries EUR 0.4 billion in future obligations. A legacy of the Deutsche Bundespost privatization, this liability is non-transferable and subject to German legislative decisions.

risks.title: Dilution risk and capital pressure via T-Mobile US
risks.summary: Deutsche Telekom actively manages its stake in T-Mobile US through share buybacks and disposals, generating EUR 7.5 billion in outflows in 2025. Any pressure on T-Mobile US share price or changes in shareholder structure (SoftBank reduced its stake to 0.42%) could affect Deutsche Telekom's ability to maintain control over its most profitable U.S. subsidiary.
risks.score_rationale: Transactions with minority shareholders of T-Mobile US reduced equity by EUR 7.5 billion in 2025 (T-Mobile US share buybacks + DT share disposals). Deutsche Telekom's stake in T-Mobile US is a strategic asset whose valuation and governance are exposed to U.S. market dynamics.

risks.title: Currency translation risk from U.S. segment consolidation
risks.summary: The consolidation of T-Mobile US exposes Deutsche Telekom to significant USD/EUR translation risk: in 2025, exchange rate effects reduced several provision items by EUR 0.1 to 0.3 billion. A sustained dollar depreciation would mechanically reduce the group's euro-denominated consolidated revenue, EBITDA, and net assets.
risks.score_rationale: USD/EUR exchange rate effects are cited multiple times as a factor reducing provisions and liabilities (–EUR 0.1 to –0.3 billion depending on the item). With T-Mobile US representing the majority of consolidated revenue, dollar depreciation structurally impacts euro-reported results.

risks.title: Telecom tower disposals and portfolio asset restructuring
risks.summary: The sale of telecom tower companies in Germany and Austria has transformed Deutsche Telekom from a passive infrastructure owner into a tenant, increasing its contractual dependency on tower operators (towercos) for mobile network deployment and maintenance, with implications for long-term operating costs.
risks.score_rationale: The disposal of GD tower companies (tower operations in Germany and Austria), completed on February 1, 2023, is still referenced in 2025 notes, indicating residual adjustments. This type of passive infrastructure sale alters cost structure and dependency on third-party operators for site access.

ai_positioning.summary: Deutsche Telekom is gradually integrating AI into its customer services and networks, without making it a major strategic pillar. The focus is on automation and operational efficiency.
evidence: Use of AI chatbots for customer service
Partnerships with cloud and AI providers
